messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: elevated 5xx error rate detected on gateway.prod (us-east-1) — 3m spike, error budget threshold breached. Runbook index: /runbooks/gateway-errors.
oncall_jen: I'm on it, grabbing context. Which service is throwing most 5xx?
maya: quick look — gateway shows surge of 502/504s between 14:02-14:06 UTC, backend fanout to model-router-1 had high latency, connection resets. Logs: `upstream_reset_peer` + increased TLS handshake times.
dave: adding: edge-nginx shows 429 for a tiny subset, but majority are 502 from model-router timeouts. Possible downstream overload or bursty client pattern.
carla: Impact? Any customer-facing errors? prod-support-bot: Incident-tracker created: INC-2026-435. Estimated affected requests ~0.6% of 1h traffic, majorly short-lived. No SLO violations yet but pages triggered due to threshold config.
oncall_jen: ok, plan: 1) throttle/route spike traffic to fallback pool, 2) enable short-term circuit-breaker on model-router, 3) roll back recent routing change (if any). Who can flip routing?
maya: I can push a routing override to send traffic to model-router-b fallback (quantized) with lower latency profile. Doing a canary now.
carla: while maya does that I'll temporarily increase the gateway proxy timeout and add 5s buffer to avoid premature 502s. Command: ``kubectl patch configmap gateway-config -p '{"data":{"proxy_read_timeout":"35s"}}' -n prod``
dave: putting an emergency circuit-breaker rule in place in envoy: set max_connections per upstream to 200 and failing fast at 95% saturation. Pushing now.
maya: canary results: 1m after override, error rate on canary path is down to baseline, overall 5xx decreased ~70%. Rolling override to 30% traffic now.
oncall_jen: monitoring — please post dashboards/urls.
maya: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/edge/requests?orgId=1&from=now-30m&to=now — look at status_code:5xx panel. Also tail logs: ``kubectl logs -f model-router-1 -n prod --since=10m | grep reset``
kim: noted client pattern: bursty traffic from a single API key (svc-data-ingest) spiked at 3k rps for ~40s, likely a runaway batch job. I've contacted the account team to throttle that key.
dave: with client throttled + routing override + cb, the 5xx is back to normal. Marking active mitigations: routing-override, gateway-timeout-bump, envoy-cb.
carla: customer impact: support queue got 12 tickets referencing "gateway error" between 14:05-14:15. No large customers reported downtime, but a few endpoints saw retries and latency increases.
oncall_jen: good. Now quick postmortem-ish notes and action items. I'll list, please ack if you own.
-- ACTION ITEMS --
1) Runbook update: add a section for model-router burst patterns and quick override snippet + exact env commands. Owner: maya.
2) Alert tuning: increase aggregation window for gateway 5xx alert to 2m and add suppression for single-key spikes. Owner: dave.
3) API key throttling automation: add auto-throttle for >1k rps sustained per key for 30s. Owner: kim.
4) Post-incident log hunt: correlate TLS handshake latency with kube node metrics (cpu/packets). Owner: carla.
5) Customer comms: draft status message for affected but non-down customers. Owner: oncall_jen.
6) Add dashboard panel showing per-api-key rps percentiles. Owner: prod-support-bot (deferred to analytics team).

oncall_jen: please ack owning items.
maya: ACK for runbook update, will push a PR within 2h with snippets and commands.
dave: ACK for alert tuning — will update alert in PagerDuty rule and create a short test.
kim: ACK for auto-throttle prototype, will post design doc by EOD.
carla: ACK for logs/metrics correlation; I'll pull node-level traces and CPU graphs.
oncall_jen: I'll draft the customer note and coordinate with support.
prod-support-bot: Creating a follow-up tracking ticket: INC-2026-435-FU, linking action items.
-- INVESTIGATION NOTES --
maya: observed model-router client connections entering TIME_WAIT at scale; tail of stack shows `async_read_some` timeouts. Hypothesis: upstream model-worker GC/stop-the-world events causing brief connection stalls -> proxies interpret as resets.
dave: kernel tcp_retries2 was normal, but socket buffer pressure spiked on a subset of nodes. Possible network egress contention.
carla: we should also check autoscaler jitter — there was a recent scale-to-zero test in that cluster earlier today, might correlate.

-- TEMPORARY MITIGATIONS APPLIED (summary) --
- Routing override to fallback pool (quantized model) rolled to 30% -> cut 5xx by ~70%
- Envoy circuit-breaker configured for failing-fast on saturated upstreams
- Gateway proxy read timeout increased to 35s to reduce premature 502s
- API key svc-data-ingest temporarily rate-limited at edge (throttled at 1k rps)

oncall_jen: final checks — is there any remaining high-risk action to revert?
maya: we should keep routing override for 1h while we observe, then gradually roll back if stable. No config rollbacks needed.
dave: will schedule the alert tuning and mark the on-call playbook updated.
carla: I'll attach node-level graphs to the follow-up ticket.
oncall_jen: thanks team. I'll close the page in 30m unless new errors reappear. Please update the follow-up ticket with your PR links and graphs.

prod-support-bot: bot note: Incident closed to paging at 15:12 UTC. Follow-up ticket INC-2026-435-FU created.
noncall_jen: postmortem next steps: 1) 72-hour incident email with timeline, 2) include remediation and alert changes, 3) schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 11:00 UTC.
maya: adding one more runbook snippet for quick override: ```bash
# route 100% of model-router traffic to fallback
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route":"model-router-b","percent":100}' \
  https://route-api.prod.internal/v1/overrides
```
carla: I'll upload logs and annotate interesting traces in the follow-up ticket.
oncall_jen: thanks all — great quick work. Closing thread after follow-ups are linked.
